'''Thomas Erle Faber''' (25 April 1927{{spnd}}27 July 2004) was an English [[physicist]] and [[Publishing|publisher]], and he was a university [[lecturer]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] for 35 years.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/tom-faber-39005.html|title=Tom Faber|date=2004-08-12|work=The Independent|access-date=2018-04-30|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Thomas Faber was born in [[London]] in 1927, the son of Sir [[Geoffrey Faber]], a don at [[All Souls College, Oxford|All Souls College]], [[Oxford]], and also the co-founder of the publishing house that later became [[Faber and Faber]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2004/sep/07/guardianobituaries.obituaries|title=Obituary: Tom Faber|last=Warner|first=Mark|date=2004-09-07|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> His maternal grandfather, Sir Erle Richards, was the former  [[Chichele Professorship|Chichele Professor of Public International Law]],  Oxford.<ref name=":0" /> Tom studied at the [[Dragon School]], Oxford and [[Oundle School|Oundle]]. He won a scholarship to [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]], [[Cambridge]] in 1945, where he studied [[Natural science|Natural Sciences]] with a specialty in physics. He moved to [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge|Corpus Christi College]] in 1953, where he became a Fellow, a position he held for the rest of his life.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
He was a lecturer in physics at the University of Cambridge from 1959 until 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/contributor/Thomas-E-Faber/3527|title=Thomas E. Faber |website=Britannica.com |language=en|access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref> He was a Life Fellow, Praelector Rhetoricus from 1956 until 1962, and the Treasurer from 1963 until 1975 at Corpus Christi College.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/?p=775|title=Corpus Christi College University of Cambridge|website=Corpus Christi College University of Cambridge|language=en|access-date=2018-04-30}}</ref>

== Research ==
Faber's academic research focused on three areas; [[superconductivity]], [[liquid metal]]s and [[liquid crystal]]s. He worked together with [[John Ziman]] to develop a theory of liquid metals.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==
Faber had two sons and two daughters from his first wife, Penelope Morton, who died in 1983; and one son and one daughter with his second wife [[Elisabeth van Houts]], whom he married in 1986.<ref name=":1" />
